title: Vectors and Matrices
question: Our path calculations already have the shape of linear algebra. What do we gain by using it?

title: A state is a vector
lead: List amplitudes in a fixed order: \(\ket0=(1,0)^T,\ \ket1=(0,1)^T\).
takeaway: The bookkeeping rules are vector addition and scaling. Amplitudes \(3/5,4/5\) give probabilities \(9/25,16/25\).
notes: A quantum system with two distinguishable configurations is a qubit; a weighted sum of configuration kets is a superposition.

title: What is the amplitude from one state to another?
steps: Through every configuration: \(\braket\phi\psi=\sum_j\braket\phi j\,\braket j\psi\), the sum rule.
takeaway: The inner product is the transition amplitude.

title: Why the conjugate?
question: Without the conjugate, what would \((\ket0+i\ket1)/\sqrt2\) give as its amplitude to itself?
answer: \(\tfrac12+\tfrac{i^2}2=0\), as if its total probability were zero. With the conjugate, \(\tfrac12+\tfrac12=1\).

title: How large can a transition amplitude be?
lead: Split \(\ket\psi\) into a part along \(\ket\phi\) and a part perpendicular to it.

title: A step is a matrix
lead: Entry \(U_{ji}=\bra jU\ket i\): column \(i\) lists where \(i\) goes.
takeaway: Multiplying the matrix by the column performs the path sums.

title: Which matrices keep total probability one?
steps: Each column has unit length (outgoing normalization).
Different columns are orthogonal (the cross-sum condition).
Two steps: \((VU)_{ki}=\sum_jV_{kj}U_{ji}\). The rightmost acts first.

title: How do we undo the square root of NOT?
question: Reversing the arrows of \(\sqrt X\) gives \(\sqrt X\) again, and \(\sqrt X\sqrt X=X\). What else must change?
answer: Also conjugate the weights. The return paths give \(|a|^2+|b|^2=1\), and the crossing paths cancel.

title: The adjoint undoes every unitary step
label: Adjoint
statement: \(\bra iU^\dagger\ket j=\bigl(\bra jU\ket i\bigr)^*\): reverse every arrow and conjugate its weight. For a unitary step, \(U^\dagger U=I\).
note: Unitary steps keep lengths and angles, \(\braket{U\chi}{U\psi}=\braket\chi\psi\). A shear also has an adjoint, but it does not undo the shear.

title: Postulates
question: Which parts of this calculation describe nature?

title: What is a state?
label: State postulate
statement: A state of a finite quantum system is a unit vector of complex amplitudes. Vectors that differ only by a global phase represent the same state.

title: How does a closed system change?
label: Evolution postulate
statement: The evolution of a closed system is unitary: \(\ket\psi\mapsto U\ket\psi\), with \(U^\dagger U=I\).
note: The mathematics forced unitarity for consistency; the postulate says nature behaves this way.

title: What does a measurement report?
label: Measurement postulate
statement: Measuring \(\ket\psi=\sum_jv_j\ket j\) in the computational basis gives \(j\) with probability \(|v_j|^2\). The state becomes \(\ket j\).

title: Measurement keeps one component
takeaway: Keep one perpendicular component, with probability equal to its squared length, and rescale it.

title: Must every measurement of |+⟩ be uncertain?
question: Measuring \(\ket+=(\ket0+\ket1)/\sqrt2\) in the computational basis gives two equally likely results. Is that true of every measurement?
answer: No. A measurement in a basis containing \(\ket+\), the X measurement, gives \(+\) with certainty. The measurement chooses the question.

title: Looking between two Hadamard steps

right.label: Measured in the middle
items: The second H gives each result half the time.

takeaway: Unitary evolution carries every amplitude forward; measurement keeps one branch.

title: What does a pair of qubits need?
steps: Independent preparations: the amplitude of \(01\) is \(ad\), by the product rule.
Composite-state postulate: every unit vector of this tensor-product space is allowed.

title: Is every joint state a product?
question: Can \((\ket{00}+\ket{11})/\sqrt2\) be written as \((a\ket0+b\ket1)\otimes(c\ket0+d\ket1)\)?
answer: No. Nonzero \(ac\) and \(bd\) force \(ad\) and \(bc\) to be nonzero, but the state has no \(01\) or \(10\) term. It is entangled.

title: Four joint configurations, four amplitudes
takeaway: Dimensions multiply: n qubits need one amplitude per bit string, 2ⁿ in all.

title: What we found
items: States are vectors; steps are matrices; the inner product is the transition amplitude.
Steps that keep total probability are unitary, and their adjoint undoes them.
Postulates: unit vectors, unitary evolution, measurement by projection, tensor products.
Measurement keeps one branch and cannot be undone.
Joint states need not be products: entanglement.
